items.question: Which rules has WELL-0001 broken in the last 12 months, and what is still open?
items.expected: Four breaches from the 11 Jun 2026 spill of 6.8 bbl: SR-01 reported after 41 h vs 24 h (REG-0001-001) leading to NOV REG-0001-002 USD 5,000 fine open; SR-02 contained after about 7 h vs 4 h (only in the June report); SR-03 clean-up verification due 10 Aug 2026 still open (REG-0001-003); RC-04 notice response due 30 Jul 2026 none recorded. Pending: root-cause analysis on flowline (MNT-0001-028, -029, -032) and the 7 Oct shut-in not recorded in the maintenance system.
items.actual:
Wells: WELL-0001.
WELL-0001 has broken four rules in the last 12 months. Protocol SR-01 was broken on 2026-06-11 because a spill of 6.8 units was reported after 41 hours, exceeding the 24-hour limit (REG-0001-001). Protocol SR-02 was broken on 2026-06-11 because the same spill was contained after approximately 7 hours, exceeding the 4-hour limit (MNT-0001-029). Protocol SR-03 was broken on 2026-06-11 because the clean-up verification for the spill was due on 2026-08-10 and is not yet closed (REG-0001-003). Protocol RC-04 was broken on 2026-06-30 because a response to a notice of violation (REG-0001-002) for a USD 5000 fine was due by 2026-07-30, but none is recorded, and the status is open.

Four items are still open for WELL-0001. The clean-up verification for Protocol SR-03 is not closed (REG-0001-003). The response to the notice of violation for Protocol RC-04 is open (REG-0001-002), with an open fine of USD 5000. A root-cause analysis is due for Manual §10 due to three corrective flowline repairs in 12 months (MNT-0001-028, MNT-0001-029, MNT-0001-032). Additionally, a planned shut-in for Manual §4 is not yet recorded in the maintenance system (CTX-0001-003).
